title.narrative: Towards a National Strategy for the use of AI and IT in the Education System

description.narrative:
Background: The conflict that erupted on 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) continues to inflict dire consequences on civilians, exacerbating the protracted economic troubles and pre-existing conflicts in the country. Thousands of people were killed and injured, millions of people fleeing their homes in search of safety, both inside Sudan and across its borders, and millions grappling with a lack of access to food, water, and other basic services. OCHA reported that since the start of the conflict, the magnitude of IDPs and refugees is on the rise - over 1 million people were forced to cross into neighbouring countries and more than 4.2 million people (845,779 Households) have been displaced to (3,929) locations across all 18 states. Approximately 25 million people, roughly half of Sudan’s population, are now vulnerable and need humanitarian assistance and protection through the end of 2023 . An estimated 19 million children in Sudan are out of school, some 6.5 million lost access to school due to the conflict, and 10,400 schools shuttered in conflict-affected areas , and 171 schools are serving as emergency shelters for the displaced population , exposing children to dangers including recruitment into armed groups, and sexual violence. The number of displaced, separated, or unaccompanied children will continue to increase as families flee. This emphasizes the need to support education to ensure its continuity and ensure that Sudanese children equitably access school and have sufficient psychosocial support in safe and child-friendly learning spaces. This calls for not only coordinated action at the national level but also a harmonized approach at the regional level. The Minister of Education (MoE) recently issued a directive for the resumption of all academic activities in all government, private, and non-governmental schools, and higher education institutions where security conditions permit, following months’ full closure of education institutions throughout the country. As requested by the MoE to support school reopening, education partners, including UNESCO, are seeking ways to ensure access and equity to safe education, and alternative learning options for learners, especially IDPs, to mitigate learning deficits and ensure continuity of learning. Sudan AI community is very much fragmented despite the efforts by national AI academics to bring together the national interest in the topic. Youth in particular before the war had interest to to join innovation labs and robotics summer classes and competitions organized for them that draw attention of all. UNESCO Khartoum in this critical time of Sudan believes that AI tools and methodologies could be of a great value for the educational crises in Sudan. Used for Out-of-Schools before in rural Sudan, “Learning at their fingertips” and “Education Can not Wait” with the support of War Child Holland software with intelligent features was piloted in Sudan 2008-2016. UNESCO contributed to the initial planning of the Arabic part of it. How AI can help once again in Sudan education hard times faced currently during the war and postwar? Is the question this project will attempt to answer. This project aims at enhancing the Sudan national Education System on the use of AI and IT in post war Sudan. The main objectives is to start the build the capacity of senior officials as well as bring together education international partners to discussions with senior officials about a strategy for Sudan.
Outcome: Sudan Educational System is enhanced on the potential use of AI and IT in Out-of-School and Literacy programs.
Output 1: Sudan Literacy program is better informed on the potential use of AI and IT. Activity 1.1: Organize brainstorming sessions on the use of AI and It in literacy programs for National professionals of Literacy, AI and IT academics and professionals. Activity 1.2: Develop a Roadmap of the integration of AI and IT in the literacy programs in Sudan with the support of National and International experts.
Implementation Strategy: To achieve this outputs, UNESCO Khartoum will work closely with UNESCO Cairo office to organize online and in person workshops to explore the how can Sudan benefit from these technologies to support literacy programs. The first workshop will be done online, grouping Sudanese academics and professionals, currently in Cairo and in Sudan, to explore the issue. This workshop is expected to include Egyptian experience and that of UNESCO in similar countries. The workshop is expected to come up with recommendations on how to move forward and who should be engaged. A second workshop will follow on what could be done exactly providing more details of a national initiative that could be supported internally and externally. This national initiative would be further elaborated into a concreate proposal with a clear budgeted road map for realization.
